svg.title: The exact identity K −A−1 = A−1E bounds its error price by PεB. For C = (K + K⊤)/2, symmetry gives error price price(C −A−1) ≤PεB and price(C) ≤ P. Schur bounds convert the error to a quadratic bound: for a matrix E whose absolute row and column sums are at most r/2, expanding the double sum and using 2|vivk| ≤v2 i + v2 k gives |v⊤Ev| ≤(r/2)∥v∥2. Since A ≤XI, A−1 ≥X−1I; this also follows by expanding the nonnegative form of w −X−1v with w = A−1v. Thus PεB ≤1/(2X) yields
